title: Benchmark runbook checklist (WIP) — FP8/INT8 sprint
linked_artifacts: Slack: #eng-infra thread 1776428891 (driver version mismatch across clusters)
body:
Purpose
- Make benchmark runs reproducible enough that we can compare: baseline vs FP8 vs INT8, kernel variants, and scheduler knob deltas.
- This is a WIP checklist; update when we find a new source of variance.

Scope
- Applies to: kernel microbench + end-to-end serving benchmarks for top hosted models during FP8/INT8 sprint.
- Primary targets: H100 + A100. Optional: L4 / cost-focused SKU when we have capacity.


0) Pre-flight: confirm what you’re running
[ ] Confirm run ID + intent (microbench vs e2e) and add a one-liner note in the daily notes doc.
    - Example: "H100 eu-central, Model X, e2e suite v3, FP8 attention on, scheduler knobs default"
[ ] Confirm the exact matrix slice assigned to you (model/GPU/workload/region).
[ ] Confirm you have clean capacity (no Dedicated pool collision). If unsure, ask Irene/Vanessa.

Required inputs to write down BEFORE you start
[ ] git SHA(s)
    - runtime repo SHA
    - benchmark-lab runner SHA
[ ] container image digest(s)
    - runtime image (not just tag)
    - runner image
[ ] cluster + node identifier
    - region / cluster name
    - instance type (H100 SXM vs PCIe if applicable)
[ ] driver + CUDA versions
    - nvidia-smi output (copy/paste)
    - nvcc --version (if present)


1) Environment pinning (most common variance root cause)
Container / code
[ ] Use the pinned images from the sprint plan (don’t "latest").
[ ] If you must use a new image, record:
    - image tag + digest
    - reason (bugfix, required CUDA, etc.)
    - link to PR or Slack thread approving change

Driver/CUDA
[ ] Verify driver matches expected range for the sprint.
    - If mismatch across clusters: stop and escalate in #eng-infra (we had false wins from this).
[ ] Confirm CUDA runtime in container is the pinned version (runner should print it).

Node isolation
[ ] Confirm exclusive access mode if available (or at least no other heavy workloads on same node).
[ ] Confirm MIG/partitioning status.
    - For these runs, default assumption is no MIG unless explicitly noted.
    - Record MIG config if present.

Power/clock/thermals
[ ] Record GPU power limit + clocks before run:
    - nvidia-smi -q -d POWER,CLOCK,PERFORMANCE
[ ] If clock locking is enabled by the runner:
    - record target graphics clock + memory clock
[ ] If clocks are NOT locked, explicitly note "unlocked" in run metadata.
[ ] Watch for thermal throttling signals:
    - log GPU temp; note if > ~80–85C sustained (shape dependent)
    - if throttle suspected, rerun on a different node or reduce contention


2) Benchmark configuration sanity
General
[ ] Confirm benchmark suite version (prompt set / distributions): "top-hosted-models-benchmark-suite-v3".
[ ] Confirm model artifact/version (registry version or model hash).
[ ] Confirm kernel mode flags (one of): baseline / fp8 / int8.
[ ] Confirm scheduler config profile (defaults vs tuned knobs).

Workload definitions (must be consistent)
[ ] Prefill-only vs decode-only vs mixed.
[ ] Mixed run must specify:
    - prompt length distribution
    - generation length (max_new_tokens)
    - concurrency target(s)
    - batching window / backpressure settings (if changed)

Stop conditions
[ ] Verify run duration or token targets match the sprint methodology.
[ ] Ensure enough samples to compute stable p50/p95 (minimum guidance):
    - e2e mixed: >= 200 requests (prefer >= 500) per configuration
    - microbench: >= 1000 iterations per shape after warmup


3) Warmup + cache hygiene (don’t skip)
[ ] Warm up GPU + kernels before measurements.
    - e2e: warmup for at least 2–5 minutes or until TTFT/TPOT stabilizes
    - microbench: discard first N iterations (N in harness config)
[ ] Confirm KV/prefix cache settings are consistent.
    - If cache is enabled, note cache hit rate (or that it was forced cold/hot).
[ ] If you’re comparing kernel modes, avoid cross-contamination:
    - restart server between modes (preferred)
    - or run in separate pods/containers


4) Running the job (execution checklist)
[ ] Run from the matrix runner when possible (preferred).
[ ] Confirm runner prints a header including:
    - git SHAs, image digests, driver/CUDA, clocks, model ID, suite version
[ ] Ensure stdout/stderr is captured to an artifact file.
[ ] Confirm metrics tagging includes at least:
    - model, gpu_sku, kernel_mode, region, build_sha

If running manually (last resort)
[ ] Copy/paste the exact command into the run notes.
[ ] Save the full config file (yaml/json) as an artifact.

Failure handling
[ ] If correctness fails in FP8/INT8:
    - capture failing shape / prompt ID
    - rerun baseline to confirm harness integrity
    - file or link to the relevant issue (INT8 shape guards have bitten us)
[ ] If perf looks too good to be true:
    - confirm driver/CUDA + clocks
    - rerun on a second node
    - compare to last known baseline on same SKU


5) Measurement sanity checks (quick gates before you upload)
[ ] Verify request error rate is near 0 (or within expected range).
[ ] Check p50/p95 TTFT + TPOT are in plausible ranges (no obvious instrumentation bug).
[ ] Check throughput/tokens/sec correlates with GPU util.
[ ] Confirm variance:
    - if run-to-run p95 swings > ~5–10% without explanation, treat as unstable
    - capture node ID, temps, and consider re-running with clock lock
[ ] Note any anomalies in the artifact notes (e.g., debug logging accidentally enabled).


6) Optional: capture profiling traces (only for triage cases)
When to capture
- Large regression or unexpected win (>10–15%) vs baseline.
- TTFT regression suspected from launch overhead or scheduler interplay.

What to capture
[ ] nsys trace for a representative case (small number of iterations; don’t profile full long run).
[ ] Include kernel names + launch configs.
[ ] Record exact command and which run produced the trace.

Where to store
[ ] Upload trace alongside artifacts in the same run folder, in a /profiles subdir.


7) Artifact packaging + upload (required)
Folder naming convention
- Use a consistent, parseable naming scheme:
  bench_<date>_<gpu>_<region>_<model>_<suite>_<kernelMode>_<runtimeSHAshort>_<runnerSHAshort>
  Example: bench_2026-02-22_H100_eu-central_modelX_suitev3_fp8_a1b2c3d_9e8f7a1

Required files
[ ] results.json (aggregates + histograms)
[ ] raw_runs/*.jsonl or equivalent raw event logs
[ ] config snapshot (resolved config)
[ ] environment.txt (nvidia-smi, driver/CUDA, clocks, node info)
[ ] stdout.log / stderr.log
[ ] notes.txt (human notes: anomalies, reruns, why)

Metadata (must be included in results or alongside)
[ ] runtime git SHA
[ ] runner git SHA
[ ] container image digests
[ ] model ID + hash/version
[ ] suite version
[ ] gpu sku + memory
[ ] driver + CUDA versions
[ ] clock lock status + target clocks
[ ] MIG status
[ ] region/cluster

Upload location
[ ] Upload to: shared_drives/engineering/serving-runtime/ (this Drive) under:
    fp8-int8/bench-artifacts/<gpu>/<date>/...
[ ] If the uploader tool is used (preferred), confirm it outputs a permalink.
[ ] Paste the permalink into:
    - the benchmark matrix sheet/doc (tab for that GPU)
    - the daily notes entry


8) Post-run: update the matrix + notify owners
[ ] Update the benchmark matrix:
    - mark case complete
    - paste key metrics (p50/p95, tokens/s, variance)
    - link to artifact folder
    - note any deviations (driver mismatch, unlocked clocks, etc.)
[ ] If you saw a regression that could impact canary:
    - notify #eng-runtime + tag Rafael (SRE canary owner)
    - include exact dimensions (model/gpu/region/kernel_mode) and artifact link


Known gotchas (add more as we learn)
- Driver/CUDA mismatch across clusters can create fake wins/losses. Always record versions.
- Debug logging/extra tracing can perturb TTFT and increase variance (double-check flags).
- Shared node contention is common during sprint windows; watch GPU util oscillations.
- Clock drift / thermal throttling on long runs can skew p95; prefer pinned clocks.
- KV cache alignment edge cases can show as decode regressions under FP8; if seen, capture shape regime and flag state.

Open questions / TODO
- Decide standard clock lock targets per SKU (H100 vs A100) and document them here.
- Define the exact minimum run count per workload (we have guidance but not a hard rule yet).
- Confirm final artifact schema after PR-19880 lands everywhere (some runners still write old fields).
- Add a short "rerun policy" section (when is a rerun mandatory vs optional).
